title: Find a Friend
story: Two explorers keep their map away from one friendly map-snatcher and travel across either end line together.
setup: Create two 10x14-yard fields. Play 2v1 on each; an attacking pair has one ball and scores by passing or dribbling over either end line under control.
instructions: The pair attacks either end line and may change direction at any time.
The defender scores by touching the ball, then immediately joins the next attacking pair.
Rotate the defender every 45 to 60 seconds even without a ball win.
Celebrate dribbling when open and passing when a friend has better space.
coach_lens: Look for the player without the ball moving where they can be seen, and the player on the ball noticing both defender and teammate. Do not require a pass count.
questions: Where can your friend see you?
When is dribbling the better choice?

simplify: Make the field wider or ask the defender to walk for the first round.
challenge: Narrow one end line to create a smaller target.
low_attendance: Play 2v1 in one field and rotate the defender often.
high_attendance: Add another 2v1 field or play 3v1; avoid a large keep-away circle.
limited_equipment: Use field lines or four shoes to mark the two scoring lines.

safety: Defenders win the ball with feet only and do not charge through players.
Leave several yards between neighboring fields.

diagram.alt: Two attackers spread around one defender between two scoring end lines; arrows show a pass and supporting run.

source.title: Plan and Create a Training Session
source.reviewer_notes: SmallSide-authored directional 2v1 applying U.S. Soccer guidance to reduce defender numbers, preserve game-like decisions and adjust space for success. No source wording or artwork reproduced.
